title: Plasmapheresis (plasma exchange)
what: A machine draws your blood, separates the liquid part, called plasma, and returns the blood cells to you. This removes harmful substances from the blood.
why: For some diseases of the immune system, blood and nervous system, and for poisoning, as decided by the doctor.
duration: a session usually takes 1 to 3 hours; a course is several sessions
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners and blood pressure pills
If you felt unwell after past procedures

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually a light breakfast before the session. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. The timing may change, and the doctor will tell you.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Loose clothes with a wide sleeve.

steps: You are weighed and your blood pressure is taken
A catheter is placed in a vein, or connected if you already have one
Blood goes into the machine and the plasma is separated
Blood cells are returned with a replacement fluid
The nurse watches your blood pressure and how you feel
At the end the system is disconnected
feel: A needle prick when the catheter is placed
Cold, or tingling of the lips or fingers: tell the nurse
after: Sit for a while before you stand up
Take it easy for the rest of the day
Drink water unless the doctor limited it
Come to the next sessions on schedule
red_flags: Rash, itching, swelling of the face or trouble breathing: call your local emergency number
Bleeding or swelling at the catheter site

faq.q: Does plasmapheresis "clean the body" for everyone?
faq.a: No. It is a medical procedure for specific conditions, and a doctor prescribes it.

faq.q: How many sessions will I need?
faq.a: It depends on the illness. Usually a course of several sessions.

reminders.text: Plasmapheresis tomorrow. Have a light breakfast, wear a wide-sleeved top, and bring your list of medicines.
